title: Why do we dream With Mark Blagrove PhD

sentences.en: It's the end of the school year and exams are approaching when you suddenly realize you forgot to drop that advanced calculus class.
sentences.zh: 当你突然意识到自己忘记退掉那门高级微积分课程时，学年已经结束，考试也迫在眉睫。

sentences.en: You haven't been to a lecture or turned in an assignment all year, and now the final exam is tomorrow and your final grade is going to be a zero.
sentences.zh: 你一整年都没去上过课，也没交过作业，而明天的期末考试将让你直接得零分。

sentences.en: The terror is real, but then you wake up and realize it was just a dream.
sentences.zh: 这种恐惧真实得可怕，但随即你醒来，发现这只是一场梦。

sentences.en: Phew!
sentences.zh: 虚惊一场！

sentences.en: Or maybe your recurring dream is that you can fly, or that you've lost your teeth, or that you found a secret room in your house that somehow you had missed for years.
sentences.zh: 或者，你反复梦到的可能是自己会飞，或是牙齿掉光了，又或者在家里发现了一个多年来从未注意过的秘密房间。

sentences.en: If you're like me, you probably wonder, where do these dreams come from, and what, if anything, might they be trying to tell you?
sentences.zh: 如果你和我一样，你可能也会好奇，这些梦究竟从何而来？它们又是否在试图向你传达些什么？

sentences.en: Psychologists have also long wondered about the origin and purpose of dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，心理学家们也一直在探究梦的起源和目的。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about some of their fascinating research and what we know and don't know about why we dream.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将探讨他们的一些迷人研究，以及我们对“为什么我们会做梦”这一问题的已知和未知。

sentences.en: So why do we dream, and do dreams serve a purpose?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们为什么会做梦？梦究竟有没有实际的作用？

sentences.en: What's the relationship between our dreams and what happens in our waking lives?
sentences.zh: 我们的梦境与现实生活中的经历之间存在着怎样的联系？

sentences.en: Why are some dreams so common, such as being unprepared for a class or showing up naked in public?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些梦会如此普遍，比如考试没准备好，或者在公众场合赤身裸体？

sentences.en: Why do some people have particularly vivid and memorable dreams, and other people say they never remember dreams at all?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人会做特别生动且令人难忘的梦，而另一些人则说他们从不记得自己做过梦？

sentences.en: Is it possible to influence the content of our dreams, or are dreams totally out of our conscious control?
sentences.zh: 我们是否有可能影响梦的内容，还是说梦完全超出了我们的意识控制？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会（American Psychological Association）的旗舰播客节目，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是主持金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Mark Blagrove, a professor of psychology at Swansea University in Wales.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是马克·布拉格罗夫（Mark Blagrove）博士，他是威尔士斯旺西大学（Swansea University）的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He studies sleep and dreaming, and his research interests include sleep and memory consolidation, the relationship between what happens in our waking life and our dream content,
sentences.zh: 他主要研究睡眠与梦境，其研究兴趣包括睡眠与记忆巩固、现实生活经历与梦境内容之间的关系，

sentences.en: and how sharing our dreams with others can build empathy and help our relationships.
sentences.zh: 以及与他人分享梦境如何能够建立同理心并改善人际关系。

sentences.en: He is the author, with Swansea University art professor Julia Lockhart, of the book The Science and Art of Dreaming, published in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 他与斯旺西大学的艺术教授朱莉娅·洛克哈特（Julia Lockhart）合著了《梦的科学与艺术》（The Science and Art of Dreaming）一书，该书已于八月出版。

sentences.en: Dr. Blagrove is a fellow of the British Psychological Society and a consulting editor to the APA journal Dreaming.
sentences.zh: 布拉格罗夫博士是英国心理学会（British Psychological Society）的资深会员，也是美国心理学会期刊《梦》（Dreaming）的咨询编辑。

sentences.en: Dr. Blagrove, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 布拉格罗夫博士，非常感谢你今天能参加我们的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me on the program, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我来参加这个节目，金。

sentences.en: So, let's start with the big question, why do we dream?
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从那个宏大的问题开始：我们为什么会做梦？

sentences.en: I know there's not one simple answer to this question, but what are some of the main reasons that scientists have proposed that people dream?
sentences.zh: 我知道这个问题没有简单的单一答案，但科学家们针对人们为什么会做梦提出了哪些主要原因？

sentences.en: Yes, there are indeed many theories for why we dream that have been put forward.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于我们为什么会做梦，人们确实提出了许多理论。

sentences.en: One of the oldest ones is that it's to do with our memories being interconnected while we sleep,
sentences.zh: 其中最古老的理论之一认为，这与我们在睡眠时记忆的相互交织有关，

sentences.en: and that we're connecting our recent experiences with past experiences in order to consolidate or make permanent and make interconnected the memories.
sentences.zh: 我们将最近的经历与过去的经历联系起来，以巩固记忆、使其永久化并交织在一起。

sentences.en: That's one very current theory, which is also quite long-standing.
sentences.zh: 这是目前非常流行的一种理论，同时也由来已久。

sentences.en: There's a threat simulation theory that holds that we practice overcoming threats in our dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 还有一种威胁模拟理论，认为我们在梦中练习克服各种威胁。

sentences.en: So, for example, like Kim, you've just said, the threat of being unprepared for an exam.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，正如金你刚才所说，那种考试没准备好的威胁。

sentences.en: Maybe we actually dream of these awful circumstances in order to practice overcoming them in a safe environment.
sentences.zh: 也许我们确实会梦到这些糟糕的情况，以便在一个安全的环境中练习如何克服它们。

sentences.en: That's another one.
sentences.zh: 这是另一种理论。

sentences.en: There's emotion processing theories as well.
sentences.zh: 此外还有情绪处理理论。

sentences.en: There's a fear reduction theory, which holds that we dream of our fears, but we dream of them in such a way that the fears then become diminished.
sentences.zh: 其中有一种恐惧减少理论，认为我们会在梦中体验恐惧，但这种梦境的呈现方式会使这些恐惧随后逐渐减弱。

sentences.en: And needless to say, there is also the epiphenomenal view, which many scientists would hold and many members of the public would hold, which is that we dream for no purpose at all.
sentences.zh: 不用说，还有一种附带现象观点，许多科学家和公众都持这种观点，即我们做梦根本没有任何目的。

sentences.en: It's just the running over of our daydreaming into our sleep.
sentences.zh: 这只是我们白天胡思乱想在睡眠中的延续。

sentences.en: Evolution hasn't got rid of it because it's not really that detrimental to us,
sentences.zh: 进化之所以没有抛弃它，是因为它对我们并没有太大的负面影响，

sentences.en: and we just have these passing images as we sleep, and they will disappear unless we wake up and remember them.
sentences.zh: 我们在睡眠中只是闪现这些稍纵即逝的画面，除非我们醒来并记住它们，否则它们就会消失。

sentences.en: In my introduction, I described a common dream being unprepared for an exam.
sentences.zh: 在开场白中，我描述了一个常见的梦——考试没准备好。

sentences.en: Many people have this dream even years after they've graduated from school, and there are other common themes such as flying or being chased or losing your teeth.
sentences.zh: 许多人在毕业多年后依然会做这样的梦，此外还有其他常见的主题，比如飞翔、被人追赶或牙齿脱落。

sentences.en: Do dream researchers have any theories about why these themes appear in so many people's dreams?
sentences.zh: 梦境研究人员对于为什么这些主题会出现在这么多人的梦中有什么理论吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there have been studies on typical themes in dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有一些关于梦中典型主题的研究。

sentences.en: That's quite correct.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: There's a problem with studying it, which is that, say, for example, the dreams of teeth falling out.
sentences.zh: 但研究这个课题存在一个问题，举个例子，比如牙齿脱落的梦。

sentences.en: Often the studies are done on these, and they find out, have you ever had such a dream?
sentences.zh: 通常针对这些开展的研究会询问受试者：你有没有做过这样的梦？

sentences.en: And so some of these dreams may actually occur only a few times in someone's lifetime, but they're actually really quite memorable.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中一些梦在某人的一生中可能只出现过几次，但它们确实让人印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: But there will indeed be common themes going through dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 不过，贯穿梦境的确会有一些共同的主题。

sentences.en: I mean, the one of finding a new room in your house is really quite striking when it happens, and a lot of people will have that a few times in their lifetime as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在房子里发现一个新房间的那种感觉在发生时确实非常震撼，许多人一生中也会经历几次。

sentences.en: And so we do have these themes, especially of threats and lucidity as well, where you realize that you're dreaming while you're dreaming.
sentences.zh: 因此我们确实有这些主题，尤其是关于威胁以及清醒梦的主题，即你在做梦时意识到自己正在做梦。

sentences.en: But overall, although we remember these, they are possibly not as common as they appear,
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，尽管我们能记住这些，它们可能并不像看上去那么普遍，

sentences.en: and that our more ordinary dreams depict our waking life and depict the circumstances and the concerns and concepts we have in our waking life,
sentences.zh: 我们更平常的梦其实是在描绘我们的现实生活，描绘我们在清醒生活中的种种境遇、担忧和概念，

sentences.en: as well as bringing in these well-known themes as well.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中也会融入这些众所周知的主题。

sentences.en: Is there some therapeutic meaning to any of this, for example?
sentences.zh: 这一切是否具有某种治疗意义？

sentences.en: I mean, I've had that dream about finding secret rooms in my house, and I'm wondering, is that symbolic of something that might be happening in my waking life?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我做过那种在房子里发现秘密房间的梦，我想知道，这是否象征着我清醒生活中可能正在发生的事情？

sentences.en: Maybe I'm asking you to be a dream analyzer at this point, but I'm just wondering what you find out from the research that you do.
sentences.zh: 也许我是在要求你此刻扮演一个解梦师，但我只是想知道从你的研究中能发现什么。

sentences.en: There is certainly the belief among therapists that if you dream of a new room or an extra room or a sofa undiscovered room in your house,
sentences.zh: 治疗师们确实普遍认为，如果你梦见自己家里出现了一个新房间、一个额外的房间或者一个未曾发现的隐藏房间，

sentences.en: then that does tie in possibly with the person discovering new things about themselves or wishing to discover things about themselves or something about their past, for example,
sentences.zh: 那么这可能确实与这个人正在发现关于自己的新事物、希望发现关于自己的新事物，或者与他们的过去有关，

sentences.en: something like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: The main thing, though, for these themes is that, as indeed Freud said, that what we need to do is to, rather than decode things as if this is what this must always mean,
sentences.zh: 然而，对于这些主题而言，最主要的一点是——正如弗洛伊德所说——我们需要做的事情不是去解码，好像某个东西永远就代表着某个固定的含义，

sentences.en: is to ask the person for their associations to it.
sentences.zh: 而是去询问当事人对该梦境的联想。

sentences.en: And what would a new house, what would a new room in your house mean to you?
sentences.zh: 一个新房子、你家里一个新房间对你来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Why, from your waking life, are you choosing that particular image to put into the dream?
sentences.zh: 为什么从你的现实生活中，你会选择那个特定的意象放进梦里？

sentences.en: So, essentially, we interpret our own dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上讲，是我们自己在解释自己的梦。

sentences.en: I mean, we kind of know what the associations are, rather than having some universal,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们其实心里清楚这些联想是什么，而不是去依赖某些普遍通用的东西，

sentences.en: like these little dream books that you can buy in the drugstore that tell you that if you dream this, it means that.
sentences.zh: 就像你在药妆店买的那种小解梦书，上面告诉你如果梦见这个就代表那个。

sentences.en: Yes, that's certainly not given any scientific credence to go by those books.
sentences.zh: 是的，依据那些书籍的做法绝对没有任何科学信誉可言。

sentences.en: Sometimes, I guess, some of the comments in them might give you an inkling of what something could possibly mean.
sentences.zh: 有时我猜，其中某些说法可能会让你隐约猜到某事可能意味着什么。

sentences.en: But on the whole, the view is that we ought to search for the memory sources of what's from our dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，大家的观点是，我们应该去寻找梦境背后的记忆来源。

sentences.en: Freud called this free association.
sentences.zh: 弗洛伊德将这称之为自由联想。

sentences.en: You think about particular components of the dream, and you work out what they're close to in your waking life or recent waking life experiences.
sentences.zh: 你会去思考梦境的特定组成部分，并弄清楚它们在你的现实生活或最近的清醒生活经验中与什么比较接近。

sentences.en: The interesting thing, though, is that although it's the person doing that, saying the associations, it's often very, very difficult for the person to do that on their own.
sentences.zh: 不过有趣的是，尽管进行这项工作并说出联想的是当事人本人，但要让当事人独自完成这件事往往非常非常困难。

sentences.en: It's actually quite useful to have somebody else ask, well, what does that mean or what does that remind you of in your recent waking life?
sentences.zh: 找另一个人来问“那是什么意思”或者“这会让你想起你最近清醒生活中的什么事”其实非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Because often we have these enormous blind spots on things, and even the experts, even the therapists, myself, others,
sentences.zh: 因为我们往往对某些事情存在巨大的盲区，甚至连专家、治疗师、我自己以及其他人，

sentences.en: we will often completely miss what an association is to a part of our dreams, unless somebody who knows us quite well points something out.
sentences.zh: 经常也会完全忽略某个梦境片段的联想究竟是什么，除非一个非常了解我们的人指出来。

sentences.en: Why do some people seem to have very vivid dreams and others don't have them or they don't remember them when they wake up?
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人似乎会做非常生动的梦，而另一些人则不做梦，或者在醒来时根本记不得？

sentences.en: Yes, there has been.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: On the fact that there is a wide difference between people, there's a wide individual difference on what's called dream recall frequency,
sentences.zh: 鉴于人与人之间存在巨大差异，在所谓的“梦境回忆频率”上存在着广泛的个体差异，

sentences.en: surveys seem to find that about a third of people have at least one dream per week.
sentences.zh: 调查发现，大约有三分之一的人每周至少做一个梦。

sentences.en: About another third have at least one dream per month, and another third have fewer than one dream per month, so they're less often.
sentences.zh: 另外大约三分之一的人每月至少做一个梦，还有三分之一的人每月做梦少于一次，频率相对较低。

sentences.en: And over the last 15 years or so, there's been a lot of work in neuroscience on what distinguishes the high from the low dream recall frequency people.
sentences.zh: 在过去大约15年里，神经科学界做了大量研究，探讨高梦recall频率人群和低梦recall频率人群的区别。

sentences.en: And one of the things that seems to happen is that there's areas, an area at the front of the brain and an area at the back of the brain,
sentences.zh: 其中似乎发生的情况之一是，大脑前部的一个区域和大脑后部的一个区域，

sentences.en: which are more active in frequent dream recallers.
sentences.zh: 在那些频繁回忆起梦境的人身上更加活跃。

sentences.en: And these areas are also active during waking life, but the important thing seems to be that they're active during sleep.
sentences.zh: 这些区域在清醒时也很活跃，但关键似乎在于它们在睡眠期间也很活跃。

sentences.en: And the dream recallers have more activity in these two areas.
sentences.zh: 而且频繁回忆梦境的人在这两个区域拥有更多活动。

sentences.en: And what has also been found is that if the area at the back of the brain, there's two lobes, one called the temporal lobe, one called the parietal lobe,
sentences.zh: 研究还发现，至于大脑后部的区域，这里有两个脑叶，一个叫颞叶，一个叫顶叶，

sentences.en: and there's a little meeting place between them.
sentences.zh: 它们之间有一个小的交汇处。

sentences.en: At that junction, if there is damage to that junction, then the person stops reporting dreams at all.
sentences.zh: 在这个交汇处，如果该部位受损，那么这个人就会完全停止报告梦境。

sentences.en: And there's a very famous book in 1997 by Mark Solms called The Neuropsychology of Dreams,
sentences.zh: 马克·索姆斯（Mark Solms）在1997年出版了一本非常著名的书，名为《梦的神经心理学》（The Neuropsychology of Dreams），

sentences.en: in which he looked back at 100 years of case studies of brain damage and found out for people having damage in this particular area and another area at the front of the brain,
sentences.zh: 他在书中回顾了长达100年的脑损伤病例研究，发现对于那些大脑这一特定区域以及大脑前部另一区域受损的人来说，

sentences.en: if they were damaged, then dream recall would stop.
sentences.zh: 如果这些部位受损，梦境回忆就会停止。

sentences.en: And so he put forward the idea that maybe there's an area at the front of the brain that generates the content of the dream,
sentences.zh: 因此他提出了这样一种观点：也许大脑前部有一个区域负责生成梦境的内容，

sentences.en: and it passes that information to the back of the brain where the imagery occurs.
sentences.zh: 并将其信息传递到发生表象的大脑后部。

sentences.en: So it seems to be that there's more activity in those areas in frequent dream recallers and possibly in the really vivid dream recallers as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，在频繁回忆梦境的人身上，这些区域似乎有更多的活动，对于那些能回忆起极其生动梦境的人来说可能也是如此。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Is that in any way connected with the way our brains process vision?
sentences.zh: 这与我们大脑处理视觉的方式有什么联系吗？

sentences.en: Because dreams are visual for the most part.
sentences.zh: 因为梦境在很大程度上是视觉化的。

sentences.en: So are our eyes actually functioning during our dreams?
sentences.zh: 那么在做梦时，我们的眼睛到底在运作吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: For many people who are sighted, yes, our dreams are visual.
sentences.zh: 对于许多视力正常的人来说，是的，我们的梦是视觉化的。

sentences.en: But the area at the back of the brain is not quite the occipital cortex, which is at the very back, which is the main visual area.
sentences.zh: 但大脑后部的那个区域并不完全是位于最后方的枕叶皮层——那是主要的视觉区。

sentences.en: It's more to do with an area to do with visual imagery, which is just in the front of that.
sentences.zh: 它更多地与紧邻其前方的一个负责视觉表象的区域有关。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are some people who have a condition in which they don't have visual imagery.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有些人患有一种不具备视觉表象能力的病症。

sentences.en: And so, for example, you know, for people who you could ask, you know, how many windows are there at the front of your house?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，你知道的，对于那些你可以询问的人，比如：你房子正面有多少扇窗户？

sentences.en: Some people will just be able to see the front of their house and count the number of window panes.
sentences.zh: 有些人能够直接“看到”他们房子的正面并数出窗玻璃的数量。

sentences.en: There are some people who just can't do that.
sentences.zh: 但有些人就是做不到这一点。

sentences.en: And it does appear that the people who have a complete lack of visual imagery also have a lack of dreaming as well.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎完全缺乏视觉表象能力的人也同样缺乏做梦的能力。

sentences.en: So it seems to be that the connection is with the imagery areas of the brain rather than the visual areas, which are more where the visual input comes in.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种联系似乎更多地指向大脑的表象区域，而不是视觉输入进来的视觉区域。

sentences.en: Now, I tend to have wildly vivid dreams that often involve well-known people.
sentences.zh: 现在，我往往会做极其生动的梦，而且这些梦里经常出现知名人士。

sentences.en: For instance, last year I dreamed I was in the Brazilian jungle hunting for vampires with Jamie Lee Curtis.
sentences.zh: 例如，去年我梦见自己和杰米·李·柯蒂斯（Jamie Lee Curtis）一起在巴西丛林里猎杀吸血鬼。

sentences.en: And I dreamed I was playing tennis with Rudy Giuliani, who was using a broken ping pong paddle.
sentences.zh: 我还梦见自己和鲁迪·朱利安尼（Rudy Giuliani）打网球，他用的是一支坏掉的乒乓球拍。

sentences.en: Now, my friends seem to enjoy it when I post some of these crazy dreams on social media.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我在社交媒体上发布其中一些疯狂的梦时，我的朋友们似乎都很喜欢。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, do people derive some kind of psychological benefit from recounting their dreams to friends and family?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，人们向朋友和家人讲述自己的梦，是否能从中获得某种心理上的好处？

sentences.en: Now, that's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: There has been over the last 20 years or so some papers on this in which, first of all, the frequency of telling dreams to friends and family has been assessed.
sentences.zh: 在过去大约20年里，有一些关于这方面的论文，首先评估了向朋友和家人讲述梦境的频率。

sentences.en: And that's been assessed for the simple reason, or one of the reasons for assessing that, is that many people say that it is very rare for that to happen.
sentences.zh: 之所以进行这种评估，其简单原因之一是许多人认为这种情况非常罕见。

sentences.en: But it really isn't that rare for it to happen.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况其实并不那么罕见。

sentences.en: It's about a third of people to about a half of people do recount their dreams once a month to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之一到一半的人会每月一次向别人讲述自己的梦。

sentences.en: So dream sharing is really quite common.
sentences.zh: 因此，分享梦境其实非常普遍。

sentences.en: And there have been several papers written on the benefits of that to people and to their friendships and relationships of sharing the dreams to other people and the greater closeness that results as a result of that.
sentences.zh: 并且已经有多篇论文探讨了向他人分享梦境给个人及其友谊和人际关系带来的好处，以及由此产生的更亲密的关系。

sentences.en: There's even then been work done on the motivations for sharing dreams and the fact that they can be shared for entertainment or out of a wish to find out more about the dream or because the other person is in the dream.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有人针对分享梦境的动机进行了研究，发现人们分享梦境可能是为了娱乐、出于想更多地了解这个梦的愿望，或者是为了梦中的另一个人。

sentences.en: And so they want to share it for that reason.
sentences.zh: 因此他们出于这个原因想要分享它。

sentences.en: But whereas all that work had been done for many years, we at Swansea and my work with Julia Lockhart, the artist I work with,
sentences.zh: 然而，尽管所有这些研究已经开展多年，我们在斯旺西以及我和我合作的艺术家朱莉娅·洛克哈特的工作中，

sentences.en: we had conducted dream groups with dream sharing because we're interested in the memory sources of dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们曾通过分享梦境来开展梦境小组活动，因为我们对梦境的记忆来源很感兴趣。

sentences.en: That was one of the reasons.
sentences.zh: 这是原因之一。

sentences.en: And we noticed that we had a greater consideration and understanding of the life circumstances of the people sharing the dreams with us as a result of public dream sharings.
sentences.zh: 我们注意到，由于公开分享梦境，我们对与我们分享梦境的人的生活境况有了更多的体谅和理解。

sentences.en: And we therefore set up experiments in which pairs of people were recruited.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们设计了实验来招募成对的人。

sentences.en: One person would tell a dream to the other one that they had.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人会把他们做的一个梦讲给另一个人听。

sentences.en: This was after recruitment.
sentences.zh: 这是在招募完成后进行的。

sentences.en: When they had their next dream, they were told, call each other up, meet, discuss the dream.
sentences.zh: 当他们做了下一个梦时，他们被告知：互相打电话、见面、讨论这个梦。

sentences.en: They were given a protocol for the discussion of the dream.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了一套讨论梦境的方案。

sentences.en: And prior to the discussions, they filled out a state empathy questionnaire that assessed how much empathy each person had towards the other person.
sentences.zh: 在讨论之前，他们填写了一份状态移情问卷，用来评估每个人对另一个人的同理心有多少。

sentences.en: And what we found was that after one to four dream sharings,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在经历了一到四次梦境分享之后，

sentences.en: there was a significant increase of empathy from the person who was listening to and discussing the dream towards the dream sharer.
sentences.zh: 倾听并讨论梦境的那个人对做梦者的同理心有了显著增加。

sentences.en: And we published a replication of that in the APA's journal, Dreaming.
sentences.zh: 我们将这一研究结果的重复实验发表在了美国心理学会的期刊《梦》（Dreaming）上。

sentences.en: We originally published it in Frontiers in Psychology.
sentences.zh: 我们最初将其发表在《心理学前沿》（Frontiers in Psychology）上。

sentences.en: And it's a very interesting finding.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的发现。

sentences.en: We didn't find a change in empathy between the person who's had the dream and is telling their dream to the other person, their empathy to the other person.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有发现做梦并将梦讲给别人听的那个人，他们对另一个人的同理心发生改变。

sentences.en: Because as you might expect, because they're concentrating on their own dream and their own life, they are not really finding out more about the other person.
sentences.zh: 正如你所预料的那样，因为他们专注于自己的梦和自己的生活，他们并没有真正去了解更多关于对方的信息。

sentences.en: So they don't have a change in empathy towards the other person.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对另一个人的同理心没有发生变化。

sentences.en: But we've certainly now shown that there's an increase in empathy, with empathy being rigorously assessed as a result of dream sharing.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在确实已经证明，通过分享梦境，在经过严格评估的同理心方面确实有所增加。

sentences.en: And what we've also suggest is that if people take it in turns to do that dream sharing, they may very well have increased empathy with each other.
sentences.zh: 我们也提出，如果人们轮流进行这种梦境分享，他们彼此之间的同理心很可能会增强。

sentences.en: And that it may indeed counteract decreases in empathy that we seem to be seeing across Western society at the moment.
sentences.zh: 并且这很可能会抵消我们目前在整个西方社会似乎看到的同理心下降的趋势。

sentences.en: Let me ask you, some of our listeners may have heard of sleep cycles and the difference between rapid eye movement or REM sleep and non-REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 请允许我问你，我们的一些听众可能听说过睡眠周期，以及快速眼动睡眠（即REM睡眠）与非快速眼动睡眠之间的区别。

sentences.en: How do REM and non-REM stages relate to dreams?
sentences.zh: REM阶段和非REM阶段与梦境有什么关系？

sentences.en: And why do we dream only during certain portions of the sleep cycle?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们只在睡眠周期的某些部分做梦？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In 1953, there was the very famous experiment, which actually by chance found that there was periodic periods of rapid eye movement during the night.
sentences.zh: 1953年，曾进行过一项非常著名的实验，该实验实际上偶然发现在夜间存在周期性的快速眼动期。

sentences.en: And over the years, it was found out that every 90 minutes, a period of rapid eye movement starts.
sentences.zh: 多年来，人们发现每隔90分钟就会开始一个快速眼动期。

sentences.en: And the periods of rapid eye movement, they're about five minutes near the start of the night, and they get as long as half an hour near the end of the night.
sentences.zh: 这些快速眼动期在夜间刚开始时大约持续五分钟，而在接近夜间结束时会延长到半小时左右。

sentences.en: And you may have five of these periods during the night.
sentences.zh: 你在夜间可能会经历五个这样的周期。

sentences.en: What was also found in 1953 was that if somebody was woken up from such a period,
sentences.zh: 1953年还有一个发现，那就是如果有人在这样一个时期被唤醒，

sentences.en: they were more likely to report a dream than if they were woken up from non-rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 他们报告梦境的可能性，要比从非快速眼动睡眠中被唤醒时更高。

sentences.en: Now, since then, we've realised that there may have been a sort of bias at the time to thinking that dreams occur in rapid eye movement sleep,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我们意识到当时可能存在一种偏见，认为梦只发生在快速眼动睡眠中，

sentences.en: and that therefore people were dismissing the dreams that occurred in non-REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 因此人们忽略了发生在非快速眼动睡眠中的梦。

sentences.en: You know, maybe they were very short, maybe they weren't very visual.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许它们很短，也许它们视觉效果不强。

sentences.en: But we now realise that dreams do occur in non-rapid eye movement sleep as well.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在意识到，梦确实也会发生在非快速眼动睡眠中。

sentences.en: And in the sleep lab, about 80% of awakenings from REM sleep result in a dream, and 50% of awakenings from non-REM sleep result in a dream being reported.
sentences.zh: 在睡眠实验室里，大约80%从快速眼动睡眠中唤醒的人会报告做梦，而50%从非快速眼动睡眠中唤醒的人会报告做梦。

sentences.en: The non-REM dreams are usually shorter, if you measure it by number of words.
sentences.zh: 如果按字数来衡量，非快速眼动期的梦通常较短。

sentences.en: And as the night progresses, you're more likely to have a dream.
sentences.zh: 随着夜晚的推移，你做梦的可能性会增加。

sentences.en: So, as you get more into the sleep across the night, there's a greater chance of the dreams occurring.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着整晚睡眠的深入，做梦的几率会更大。

sentences.en: And there is this difference, though, between the sleep stages in the dreams being reported.
sentences.zh: 不过，不同睡眠阶段所报告的梦境确实存在这种差异。

sentences.en: But we do seem to be able to report a dream from most parts of the night.
sentences.zh: 但我们在夜晚的大多数时段似乎都能够报告梦境。

sentences.en: We can never quite tell whether somebody is going to report a dream or not, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我们永远无法确切判断某人是否会报告梦境。

sentences.en: And an interesting recent finding was that there was an interesting recent finding which assessed people's EEG across the night, woke people up repeatedly during the night.
sentences.zh: 最近有一个有趣的发现，即评估人们整晚的脑电图，并在夜间重复唤醒他们。

sentences.en: And it was able to be predicted eventually by an algorithm that was developed whether the person would wake up with a dream or not with a dream.
sentences.zh: 最后，通过开发的算法，可以预测此人醒来时是否会带着梦境。

sentences.en: And this was the finding that there's an area, again, like I said earlier on, near the back of the brain, which if that is very active,
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，研究发现大脑后部有一个区域，如果这个区域非常活跃，

sentences.en: then the person is more likely to report a dream.
sentences.zh: 那么此人就更有可能报告梦境。

sentences.en: So, we do seem to report dreams throughout the night, but it seems to turn off and on, and it's more likely to occur in rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们似乎整晚都在报告梦境，但它似乎时断时续，且更容易发生在快速眼动睡眠中。

sentences.en: And it seems to occur when this area, which has been called the hot zone, is active at the back part of the brain.
sentences.zh: 而且它似乎发生在大脑后部这个被称为热区的区域活跃的时候。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk for a minute about how you study dreams, because I know you work in a lab and people will come in and sleep.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们花一分钟聊聊如何研究梦，因为我知道你在实验室工作，人们会来这里睡觉。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you'll wake them during the course of a night.
sentences.zh: 听起来你会在夜间叫醒他们。

sentences.en: How do you determine when you're going to wake somebody, what you're going to ask them?
sentences.zh: 你是如何决定何时唤醒某人，以及你要问他们什么的？

sentences.en: And doesn't that somehow bias, in essence, what's happening?
sentences.zh: 这难道不会在本质上对发生的事情产生某种偏见吗？

sentences.en: It's different from if you were just at home in your own bed, sleeping, and maybe you had five dreams that night and you could tell them in the morning.
sentences.zh: 这和你独自在家里的床上睡觉不同，也许你那天晚上做了五个梦，早上还能讲出来。

sentences.en: Yes, that's very true.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常正确。

sentences.en: There is a level of bias there that can happen.
sentences.zh: 那里确实存在一定程度的偏见。

sentences.en: The most famous one, and this was discovered in the early 1960s, is that if people are in the sleep lab and undergoing an experiment and their dreams are being collected,
sentences.zh: 最著名的一个发现是在20世纪60年代初发现的：如果人们在睡眠实验室里参与实验并且正在收集他们的梦，

sentences.en: about a third of the dreams refer to being in the sleep lab.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之一的梦涉及身处睡眠实验室。

sentences.en: So, the fact that you're in the sleep lab does actually affect the content of the dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，身处睡眠实验室这一事实确实会影响梦的内容。

sentences.en: Now, it doesn't affect the whole dream, thankfully, and so we don't just get dreams which are solely about the sleep lab.
sentences.zh: 值得庆幸的是，它并没有影响整个梦，所以我们的梦并非全都是关于睡眠实验室的。

sentences.en: But there is that what you could call even contamination going on, and there is the possibility, really, that the natural course of a dream that would have occurred,
sentences.zh: 但你可以称之为一种污染的现象确实存在，并且确实存在这样一种可能性：正如你刚才所说，

sentences.en: as you've just said, if somebody was sleeping at home, doesn't occur in the lab, or doesn't occur to such an extent in the lab.
sentences.zh: 如果一个人在家睡觉，原本会自然发生的梦，在实验室里并没有发生，或者在实验室里没有那么大程度地发生。

sentences.en: But we do have an issue, really, of needing to work in the lab, because that's the way of making sure, for example, that you've got a REM sleep dream of a particular length,
sentences.zh: 但我们确实面临一个问题，即我们需要在实验室里工作，因为这是确保你获得特定长度（例如10分钟）的快速眼动睡眠梦的方法。

sentences.en: let's say 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 比方说10分钟。

sentences.en: You wait for the person to go into rapid eye movement sleep, and then you start the stopwatch going, and then wake them, say, 10 minutes later or 5 minutes later.
sentences.zh: 你等待受试者进入快速眼动睡眠，然后启动秒表，接着在比如10分钟或5分钟后叫醒他们。

sentences.en: So, from the point of view of getting the robust results, we have to be in the sleep lab, but that is correct, there can be some bias occurring.
sentences.zh: 因此，从获得可靠结果的角度来看，我们必须在睡眠实验室里进行，但这是对的，确实可能会产生一些偏差。

sentences.en: Note, though, one thing, which is that, for example, some of the studies we do, we wish to compare people's REM dreams with their non-REM dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 不过请注意一点，例如，我们做的一些研究旨在比较人们的快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦。

sentences.en: Of course, the person doesn't know whether they've had a REM dream or a non-REM dream.
sentences.zh: 当然，当事人并不知道自己做的是快速眼动梦还是非快速眼动梦。

sentences.en: So, we can still do studies where we show them their dream, and we get ratings of the dream, for example, such as of how long it was, or how much emotion there is in it.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们仍然可以开展研究，向他们展示他们的梦，并对梦进行评分，例如它的长度或其中包含多少情绪。

sentences.en: Or, indeed, for some of the studies we've done, how far away, how far back in their diaries they've been keeping, does the dream refer to?
sentences.zh: 或者，在我们做过的一些研究中，梦所涉及的内容回溯到了他们日记里多久以前的事？

sentences.en: And what we find is that there's a time course difference between REM and non-REM dreams on the memory sources for the dream.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦在梦的记忆来源方面存在时间进程上的差异。

sentences.en: And in that instance, there's less of a bias, I guess, because you're looking at someone's REM and non-REM dreams,
sentences.zh: 我想，在这种情况下，偏差会比较小，因为你是在观察某人的快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦，

sentences.en: and it's only the experimenters that would know which dream is which.
sentences.zh: 而且只有实验人员才知道哪个梦是哪个梦。

sentences.en: Are there qualitative differences in REM and non-REM dreams?
sentences.zh: 快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦在质量上有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Yes, there are qualitative differences.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们在质量上确实有差异。

sentences.en: The non-REM dreams are shorter.
sentences.zh: 非快速眼动梦更短。

sentences.en: They may have fewer emotions, fewer characters, fewer scenes.
sentences.zh: 它们可能包含较少的情绪、较少的人物、较少的场景。

sentences.en: And there is a dispute, a debate goes on about that, because if you control for the length of the dream in words, then short,
sentences.zh: 对此存在争议和争论，因为如果你按梦的字数长度进行控制，那么短小的、

sentences.en: rapid-eye movement sleep dreams are very similar to long, non-rapid-eye movement dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 快速眼动睡眠梦与漫长的、非快速眼动睡眠梦非常相似。

sentences.en: And so, one theory says that actually the REM and non-REM dreams only differ in terms of how long they are.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一种理论认为，实际上快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦仅在长度上有所不同。

sentences.en: There's that difference.
sentences.zh: 确实存在这种差异。

sentences.en: And they don't actually have any qualitative difference.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上没有任何质的区别。

sentences.en: They don't really have any qualitative difference.
sentences.zh: 它们确实没有任何质的区别。

sentences.en: As you get nearer to the end of the night, the non-REM dreams start to look more like REM dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 随着接近夜晚结束，非快速眼动梦开始变得越来越像快速眼动梦。

sentences.en: They start to get longer.
sentences.zh: 它们开始变长。

sentences.en: They start to get more bizarre and with more characters.
sentences.zh: 它们开始变得更加怪异，出现更多的人物。

sentences.en: And so, there are all of these multitude of factors coming in that affect the dreams across the night.
sentences.zh: 因此，有大量各种各样的因素介入，影响着整晚的梦境。

sentences.en: Let's talk about nightmares.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈噩梦。

sentences.en: What purpose do psychologists think they serve?
sentences.zh: 心理学家认为它们起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: Yes, there's a whole range of thoughts about nightmares.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于噩梦有各种各样的看法。

sentences.en: I mean, there is the medical view and clinical psychology view, which is that nightmares are something that possibly need treating if the person is really distressed by them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，存在医学观点和临床心理学观点，即如果一个人被噩梦严重困扰，噩梦可能是需要治疗的。

sentences.en: There's a method for doing that, imagery rehearsal therapy, in which the person imagines their nightmare and images their nightmare during the day with changed parts to it.
sentences.zh: 有一种治疗方法叫做意象排练疗法，即患者在白天想象并构想他们的噩梦，并在其中加入改变的情节。

sentences.en: And that decreases the number of nightmares that they have.
sentences.zh: 这会减少他们做噩梦的次数。

sentences.en: And that type of approach to nightmares would see them as a disorder of sleep, you know, much as apnea is a disorder of sleep or insomnia, say.
sentences.zh: 这种对待噩梦的方法会将它们视为一种睡眠障碍，你知道的，就像呼吸暂停或失眠一样。

sentences.en: And so, it would see it in terms of how do we reduce the number of nightmares that are occurring to a person.
sentences.zh: 因此，它会从如何减少一个人做噩梦的次数这一角度来看待这个问题。

sentences.en: There are then theories of nightmares.
sentences.zh: 然后就有了关于噩梦的各种理论。

sentences.en: There's one even that says that in nightmares, nightmares are beneficial to you because they are the place where you practice the most severe threats to yourself.
sentences.zh: 甚至有一种理论认为噩梦对你有益，因为它们是你练习应对自身最严重威胁的场所。

sentences.en: And it may be uncomfortable to the individual, but like pain, it's actually useful.
sentences.zh: 对个人来说这可能让人不舒服，但就像疼痛一样，它其实是有用的。

sentences.en: So, there is an evolutionary theory of nightmares, which says that they are beneficial.
sentences.zh: 因此，存在一种关于噩梦的进化理论，认为它们是有益的。

sentences.en: Another theory says that dreams in general have functions, you know, possibly to do with memory and is one possibility or emotion processing.
sentences.zh: 另一种理论认为，梦总体上具有某些功能，你知道的，可能与记忆有关（这是一种可能性）或者是情绪处理。

sentences.en: And that when we have a nightmare, it's been too much for the mind during the night.
sentences.zh: 而当我们做噩梦时，说明夜间的心智已经不堪重负。

sentences.en: And so, the nightmare is a sign that the function of dreaming has failed.
sentences.zh: 因此，噩梦是做梦功能失效的一个信号。

sentences.en: So, there are all those theories.
sentences.zh: 所以，存在所有这些理论。

sentences.en: There's been an interesting recent paper about the people who have more frequent nightmares react less to negative photographs that they're shown when they are awake.
sentences.zh: 最近有一篇有趣的论文指出，经常做噩梦的人在清醒时看到消极照片时，反应没有那么强烈。

sentences.en: And one possibility there is that the frequent nightmares attune people to nasty, horrible images so that we're less bothered by them when we're awake.
sentences.zh: 其中的一种可能性是，频繁的噩梦使人们对令人讨厌、可怕的图像产生了适应，这样我们在清醒时就不会被它们过分困扰。

sentences.en: So, there's even that pro-function view that nightmares have a function in that point of view.
sentences.zh: 因此，甚至还有这种支持功能论的观点，即从那个角度来看噩梦具有某种功能。

sentences.en: How do you study nightmares?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何研究噩梦的？

sentences.en: It seems like it wouldn't be ethical to try to induce nightmares in a sleep lab.
sentences.zh: 在睡眠实验室里试图诱发噩梦似乎是不道德的。

sentences.en: So, how do you look at nightmares?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们是如何研究噩梦的呢？

sentences.en: Yes, that's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: It would almost certainly be unethical to actually cause someone to have nightmares, yes.
sentences.zh: 故意导致某人做噩梦几乎肯定是违背伦理的，是的。

sentences.en: What's usually done is naturalistic experiments.
sentences.zh: 通常的做法是进行自然主义实验。

sentences.en: So, there was, for example, in 1989, an earthquake in California.
sentences.zh: 例如，1989年加利福尼亚发生了一场地震。

sentences.en: And people living in California were studied as a result of that.
sentences.zh: 因此居住在加利福尼亚的人们成为了研究对象。

sentences.en: And it was found that the people in California were having many more nightmares than were people in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，加利福尼亚的人们比亚利桑那州的人们做了更多的噩梦。

sentences.en: And they weren't just having nightmares about earthquakes, but they were having nightmares in general.
sentences.zh: 他们做的不仅仅是关于地震的噩梦，而是各种各样的噩梦。

sentences.en: And so, what you can do is get people who've been through a traumatic incident and study the increase in nightmares that results.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以做的是找到经历过创伤事件的人，并研究由此导致的噩梦增加情况。

sentences.en: Another possibility is, rather than talking about extreme populations like that, is that some of the studies that we've done have involved getting a large sample of people,
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是，我们进行的一些研究不涉及讨论极端人群，而是招募一大批受试者，

sentences.en: say 200 people, asking them how often they have nightmares and correlating that with their levels of anxiety and depression and stress.
sentences.zh: 比如200人，询问他们做噩梦的频率，并将其与他们的焦虑、抑郁和压力水平进行关联分析。

sentences.en: And what you find then is moderate correlations between anxiety, stress, depression, and having nightmares.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会发现焦虑、压力、抑郁与做噩梦之间存在中等程度的相关性。

sentences.en: So, you can do studies in a naturalistic sense there that find out why some people have nightmares more than others.
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以在自然主义的意义上开展研究，找出为什么有些人比其他人更容易做噩梦。

sentences.en: We've recently done work on a very, very interesting personality trait of sensory processing sensitivity, that some people are highly sensitive persons and other people aren't.
sentences.zh: 我们最近对一种非常非常有趣的个性特质——感觉处理敏感性——进行了研究，即有些人是高度敏感的人，而另一些人则不是。

sentences.en: And there's a very interesting 27-item scale for measuring that.
sentences.zh: 有一个非常有趣的27项量表用于测量这一点。

sentences.en: Elaine Aron was the divisor of that.
sentences.zh: 伊莱恩·阿伦是该量表的发明者。

sentences.en: And what we found is that being a highly sensitive person predisposes you to have nightmares if you're stressed.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果你感到压力山大，作为一个高度敏感的人会使你更容易做噩梦。

sentences.en: But if you are low on sensory processing sensitivity and you have stress, it doesn't cause nightmares for them.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的感觉处理敏感性较低并且承受压力，就不会引发噩梦。

sentences.en: So, it's a confound.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个混杂因素。

sentences.en: It's an interaction between sensory processing sensitivity.
sentences.zh: 这是与感觉处理敏感性相关的一种交互作用。

sentences.en: Some people are easily overwhelmed by stimuli and they jump at sounds.
sentences.zh: 有些人很容易被刺激压倒，听到声音就会吓一跳。

sentences.en: And they're possibly more thoughtful, philosophical people.
sentences.zh: 他们可能更具思想性、哲学性。

sentences.en: People who are highly sensitive persons, if they're put into a stressful situation, are more likely to respond with nightmares as a result.
sentences.zh: 高敏感人群如果被置于压力情境中，因此而以噩梦作为反应的可能性更高。

sentences.en: Is dreaming unique to humans or do other animals dream as well?
sentences.zh: 做梦是人类独有的，还是其他动物也会做梦？

sentences.en: Now, that is interesting about what do animals do?
sentences.zh: 现在，关于动物会做什么这个问题很有趣，

sentences.en: Because we've often, many people, and myself including with my cats, you can see cats and dogs moving as if they're trying to catch something.
sentences.zh: 因为我们经常看到——很多人，包括我自己和我的猫——猫和狗在睡觉时的动作看起来就像在试图抓住什么东西。

sentences.en: They do rhythmic movements or other type of movements during their sleep.
sentences.zh: 它们在睡眠中会做出有节奏的动作或其他类型的动作。

sentences.en: So, there is that type of circumstantial evidence that non-human animals might be having dreams that they're reacting to during the night.
sentences.zh: 因此，存在这种类型的间接证据，表明非人类动物可能也会做它们在夜间做出反应的梦。

sentences.en: That is very, very plausible.
sentences.zh: 这非常非常貌似合理。

sentences.en: After all, these animals quite possibly have a level of possibly even daydreaming, you could say, similar to us or imagery going on similar to us.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这些动物很可能具有与我们相似的某种白日梦水平，或者说类似于我们的意象活动。

sentences.en: And so, possibly it would seep over into their sleep to have dreams as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，这很可能会蔓延到它们的睡眠中，让它们也做梦。

sentences.en: There is a debate within child development literature on dreaming as to whether children have dreams which are quite like adults, you know, bizarre dreams with lots of characters,
sentences.zh: 在儿童发展关于做梦的文献中存在一场争论，即儿童是否会做类似于成年人的梦，例如有许多角色的怪异梦境，

sentences.en: for example.
sentences.zh: 比如说。

sentences.en: Or do children, other findings are that children have very, very rudimentary dreams for the first few years of life, not really with other characters in.
sentences.zh: 或者还有其他发现表明，儿童在生命的最初几年里只有非常非常初步的梦，里面并没有真正的其他角色。

sentences.en: Or they may just dream about pets or animals or bodily states.
sentences.zh: 或者他们可能只是梦到宠物、动物或身体状态。

sentences.en: And from that point of view, which is the cognitive and neurocognitive view of dreaming, humans develop the skill of dreaming.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，也就是关于做梦的认知和神经认知观点，人类发展出了做梦的技能。

sentences.en: And we have to develop it up until the time when we're in our teaMs.
sentences.zh: 我们必须不断发展它，直到我们十几岁的时候。

sentences.en: Now, from that point of view, if the neurocognitive people are correct, Bill Dolmhoff at University of California, Santa Cruz is one of the most famous ones for that,
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，如果神经认知学派的人是正确的——加州大学圣克鲁兹分校的比尔·多尔姆霍夫是其中最著名的人物之一，

sentences.en: then you wouldn't really expect animals to have very much more than rudimentary dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 那么你真的不会期望动物会拥有比初步梦境多太多的东西。

sentences.en: Because according to him, and the neurocognitive point of view, even young children have very, very rudimentary dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 因为根据他和神经认知学派的观点，即使是很小的孩子也只有非常非常初步的梦。

sentences.en: So, we can doubt that animals would have very much going on like that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们可以怀疑动物是否会有太多那样的活动。

sentences.en: So, you mentioned watching your cats when they're sleeping and they may move their legs as if they maybe are chasing something in their dream.
sentences.zh: 所以，你提到观察你的猫睡觉时，它们可能会动腿，好像在梦里追逐什么东西。

sentences.en: I'm wondering about the issue of sleepwalking.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇梦游的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, we know people do that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们知道人们会那样做。

sentences.en: How does sleepwalking relate to dreaming?
sentences.zh: 梦游与做梦有什么关系？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about rapid eye movement sleep is that,
sentences.zh: 关于快速眼动睡眠，有趣的事情之一是，

sentences.en: as well as the brain being very active during REM sleep and the eyes having these periodic bursts during the sleep, is that our muscle tone is almost completely gone.
sentences.zh: 除了大脑在快速眼动睡眠期间非常活跃、眼睛在睡眠期间有这些周期性的爆发外，我们的肌肉张力也几乎完全消失了。

sentences.en: So, our lungs are still working and our hearts are still working, but very little else.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的肺仍在工作，心脏仍在工作，但几乎没有别的了。

sentences.en: And so,
sentences.zh: 因此，

sentences.en: what's been found is that people sleep talk and sleepwalk during non-rapid eye movement sleep because that's the time when the muscles that are needed to do that are working.
sentences.zh: 人们发现在非快速眼动睡眠期间会说梦话和梦游，因为那是执行这些动作所需的肌肉正在工作的时期。

sentences.en: The usual view is that the people who are sleepwalking are not dreaming of what they are doing.
sentences.zh: 通常的观点是，梦游的人并没有在梦中经历他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: That's the usual view there.
sentences.zh: 那是通常的看法。

sentences.en: And the usual view of sleep talking is similarly that the person is not having a dream which is related to the talking.
sentences.zh: 对说梦话的普遍看法同样是，当事人并没有做与说话相关的梦。

sentences.en: The one exception to all of this is what's called REM behavior disorder, which is really quite rare.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切中唯一的例外被称为快速眼动睡眠行为障碍，这其实相当罕见。

sentences.en: But in that, what's called atonia, the lack of muscle tone that occurs during rapid eye movement sleep is got rid of.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，所谓的肌张力丧失（即快速眼动睡眠期间发生的肌肉张力缺失）消失了。

sentences.en: And so, the person can act out dreams and can actually sometimes act out quite violent dreams and this sometimes gets to the notice of the authorities and criminal authorities
sentences.zh: 因此，这个人可以把梦境演绎出来，有时甚至可以把相当暴力的梦境演绎出来，有时这会引起当局和刑事司法部门的注意，

sentences.en: because there is the possibility sometimes of violent acts being committed by somebody with REM behavior disorder.
sentences.zh: 因为患有快速眼动睡眠行为障碍的人有时可能会实施暴力行为。

sentences.en: But that disorder is really quite rare, whereas sleepwalking and sleep talking are quite common non-REM conditions.
sentences.zh: 但这种障碍确实非常罕见，而梦游和说梦话则是相当常见的非快速眼动睡眠状况。

sentences.en: I want to talk a little bit about lucid dreaming,
sentences.zh: 我想稍微谈谈清醒梦，

sentences.en: which is the dreams where people are aware that they're dreaming and that they might even be able to influence what happens in the dream to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们意识到自己在做梦，甚至可能在一定程度上影响梦中发生的事情的梦。

sentences.en: What can you tell our audience about lucid dreaming?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们的观众讲讲清醒梦吗？

sentences.en: How does it happen?
sentences.zh: 它是如何发生的？

sentences.en: How common is it?
sentences.zh: 它有多常见？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lucid dreaming is really quite rare in that about half the population in Europe and North America have had a lucid dream once in their lifetime.
sentences.zh: 清醒梦其实相当罕见，欧洲和北美大约有一半的人在一生中曾有过一次清醒梦。

sentences.en: And about 20% of the population have a lucid dream about once every month.
sentences.zh: 大约20%的人大约每个月会做一次清醒梦。

sentences.en: And so, they're relatively rare.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们相对罕见。

sentences.en: In the sleep lab,
sentences.zh: 在睡眠实验室里，

sentences.en: what's been found is it's about 2% to 3% of rapid eye movement sleep dreams are lucid dreams where somebody actually knows they're dreaming and the dream continues.
sentences.zh: 研究发现，大约2%到3%的快速眼动睡眠梦是清醒梦，此时当事人实际上知道自己在做梦，且梦境仍在继续。

sentences.en: And so, as well as knowing that it's a dream, they could, if they chose to, affect the content of the dream.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了知道这是一个梦之外，他们如果选择的话，还可以影响梦的内容。

sentences.en: That can affect the plot or introduce characters to the dream or in a recent one that I had, decide to fly.
sentences.zh: 那可以影响情节、将人物引入梦中，或者像我最近做过的一个梦那样，决定飞翔。

sentences.en: And so, that can happen as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，这种情况也会发生。

sentences.en: So, they really are quite rare, but very interesting when they do happen.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们确实相当罕见，但一旦发生却非常有趣。

sentences.en: Because they happen in rapid eye movement sleep, there is a view that the brain needs to be really quite active in order to have them.
sentences.zh: 因为它们发生在快速眼动睡眠期间，所以有一种观点认为，大脑需要保持相当高的活跃度才能产生这种梦。

sentences.en: They don't really seem to occur in non-rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎不会在非快速眼动睡眠中发生。

sentences.en: And one of the main methods for inducing lucid dreams is to have the person wake up a couple of hours earlier than they would normally wake.
sentences.zh: 诱导清醒梦的主要方法之一，就是让当事人比平时早醒几个小时。

sentences.en: Get up, walk around, do things for an hour or two, and then go back to sleep for a nap.
sentences.zh: 起床，四处走动，活动一两个小时，然后重新上床睡个回笼觉。

sentences.en: And because they've then delayed the second part of their sleep or the later part of their sleep, the brain is really quite active then.
sentences.zh: 而且由于他们随后推迟了第二阶段或后半段的睡眠，此时的大脑其实非常活跃。

sentences.en: And so, what's found is that this, what's called wake back to bed method, is very good for inducing lucid dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们发现这种被称为“回床唤醒法”的方法，对于诱导清醒梦非常有效。

sentences.en: So, the first thing is we seem to think it's to do with a very active brain causing you to be lucid.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先我们倾向于认为这与高度活跃的大脑使你保持清醒有关。

sentences.en: The second thing is that some people may just sometimes notice that something is weird or incongruous in a dream and say, ah, am I awake or am I dreaming?
sentences.zh: 其次，有些人有时可能会注意到梦中有什么诡异或不协调的地方，然后会想：啊，我是醒着还是在做梦？

sentences.en: And indeed, there's even a method developed around that, which is a reality checking method where people check reality in the day.
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至还围绕这一点开发出了一种方法，即现实检验法，人们在白天会进行现实检验。

sentences.en: They continually ask themselves, am I awake or am I dreaming?
sentences.zh: 他们不断地问自己：我是醒着还是在做梦？

sentences.en: And hopefully, it can carry over into their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 希望这能延续到他们的梦境中。

sentences.en: So, a combination of all those reasons cause people to have lucid dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些原因结合起来，导致人们做清醒梦。

sentences.en: There is a personality measure of internal locus of control, which we found is related to lucid dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 有一个衡量内在控制点的个性指标，我们发现它与清醒梦有关。

sentences.en: Internal locus of control people believe that they're in charge of their own life.
sentences.zh: 具有内在控制点的人认为自己能够主宰自己的生活。

sentences.en: They also believe that other people are quite in charge of their own lives as well, or ought to be.
sentences.zh: 他们也认为其他人同样能够主宰自己的生活，或者理应如此。

sentences.en: And people who are high on internal locus of control tend to have more lucid dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 内在控制点得分较高的人往往会做更多的清醒梦。

sentences.en: So, it's as if that personality feature creeps over into their dreams and causes them to be aware of dreaming and even wanting to control the dream.
sentences.zh: 所以，就好像这种个性特征潜入了他们的梦中，让他们意识到自己在做梦，甚至想要掌控梦境。

sentences.en: Is it something that you can teach yourself, though, over time?
sentences.zh: 不过，随着时间的推移，这是可以通过自我学习掌握的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it can be taught.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是可以学会的。

sentences.en: If people are very interested in lucid dreams, indeed, what can sometimes happen is people can hear about lucid dreams for the first time,
sentences.zh: 如果人们对清醒梦非常感兴趣，事实上，有时会出现这种情况：人们第一次听说清醒梦，

sentences.en: so they know they exist, and that can cause people to start having a lucid dream because they know that they exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们知道清醒梦的存在，而这就会促使人们开始做清醒梦，因为他们知道清醒梦是存在的。

sentences.en: Also, if people fall asleep wanting to have a lucid dream, that can help them to have one.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果人们带着想做清醒梦的愿望入睡，这也会帮助他们实现。

sentences.en: There's the wait-back-to-bed method that I've mentioned earlier on, and there's now technological measures,
sentences.zh: 除了我刚才提到的回床唤醒法之外，现在还有一些技术手段，

sentences.en: either in the sleep lab or you can buy these, in which, for example, there'll be a mask that's put on your face,
sentences.zh: 无论是在睡眠实验室里还是你买得到的设备，例如，有一种面罩戴在你的脸上，

sentences.en: and that detects whether your eyes are moving during sleep, and when the eyes are moving, it flashes red lights at you,
sentences.zh: 它能检测你的眼睛在睡眠中是否在动；当眼球转动时，它会向你闪烁红光，

sentences.en: and the red lights cause the dream to change, either with red objects come in or a red hue goes towards the entire environment.
sentences.zh: 而红光会促使梦境发生变化，要么是出现红色的物体，要么是整个环境中弥漫着一层红晕。

sentences.en: And the person may then realize that they're dreaming and can then question,
sentences.zh: 然后当事人可能会意识到自己在做梦，并开始产生疑问：

sentences.en: ah, I am dreaming, and they know they're having a lucid dream, and the dream carries on as a lucid dream.
sentences.zh: 啊，我在做梦。他们知道自己正在做清醒梦，于是梦境便作为清醒梦继续进行下去。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, there are some things that we do in life that I think we just don't tend to do in dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们在生活中做的一些事情，我认为在梦中往往是不会做的。

sentences.en: For example, I don't think people do math in their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 例如，我认为人们不会在梦里做数学题。

sentences.en: What are some of the things that we do in our waking lives that we just don't ever dream about?
sentences.zh: 我们在现实生活中做过，却绝对不会梦到的事情有哪些？

sentences.en: Yes, that is interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: There's a very famous paper by Ernest Hartman, who was a very major psychiatrist and dream researcher, and he wrote a paper in 1995 called We Do Not Dream of the Three R's.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·哈特曼（Ernest Hartman）曾发表过一篇非常著名的论文，他是一位非常重要的精神病学家和梦境研究员，他在1995年发表了一篇名为《我们不梦见三R（读、写、算）》的论文。

sentences.en: So we don't dream of reading, writing, and arithmetic.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不会梦到阅读、写作和算术。

sentences.en: And even though we spend a lot of the time doing those things in our waking life,
sentences.zh: 尽管我们在现实生活中花了很多时间做这些事情，

sentences.en: they may just not be interesting enough to occur in our dreams, unless, of course, there's some reason to have it there in the dream.
sentences.zh: 但它们可能不够有趣，以至于不会出现在我们的梦中，除非当然有什么原因让它们出现在梦里。

sentences.en: So despite the fact that we spend so much time doing these things, they don't show up in our dreams very much.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管我们花了很多时间做这些事情，但它们并没有在我们的梦中大量出现。

sentences.en: Now, the interesting thing there is, though, that that was a sort of observational study that Ernest Hartman did.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那只是欧内斯特·哈特曼做的一项类似观察性的研究。

sentences.en: If you actually want to do an experimental study to show that what's emotional to you in waking life is more likely to come into your dreams,
sentences.zh: 如果你实际上想做一个实验研究，来证明现实生活中对你而言具有情感色彩的事情更有可能进入你的梦中，

sentences.en: that's really quite intricate to do that.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点其实相当复杂。

sentences.en: And so the way that that's done is that the way that various teams have done that is to get people to keep a diary.
sentences.zh: 所以具体做法是，各个团队所采用的方法是让受试者记日记。

sentences.en: And in the diary, they record what's happened to them during the day and the levels of emotion of what happens to them during the day.
sentences.zh: 在日记中，他们记录白天发生的事情以及白天发生事情时的情感水平。

sentences.en: Then they record any dreams that they have.
sentences.zh: 然后他们记录自己做的任何梦。

sentences.en: And what they do next is they compare, they're asked to compare the diaries to their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 他们接下来要做的是进行对比，要求他们将日记与梦境进行对照。

sentences.en: And they're asked, okay, what in the diary ended up in your dream?
sentences.zh: 他们被问到：好吧，日记里的什么内容最终进入了你的梦里？

sentences.en: So the person is not allowed to say, ah, this came from my dream.
sentences.zh: 因此，当事人不允许说：啊，这个是来自我的梦。

sentences.en: I know where that's from, but they hadn't put it in the diary.
sentences.zh: 我知道这出自哪里，但他们之前并没有把它写进日记里。

sentences.en: This is very strictly and rigorously controlled.
sentences.zh: 这是受到非常严格和严密控制的。

sentences.en: So you can only use the things that were in your diary.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能使用日记里记录过的事情。

sentences.en: And what's found then is that the items in diaries that go into dreams tend to be more emotional than the items in diaries that don't go into the dream.
sentences.zh: 人们随后发现，日记中进入梦境的条目往往比未进入梦境的条目更具情感色彩。

sentences.en: And so that's, in a way, the evidence that we tend to dream of what's emotional to us.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这就是我们倾向于梦到对我们有情感意义的事物的证据。

sentences.en: We did a follow-up study to that at Swansea because those dreams in those studies were dreams that people reported at home.
sentences.zh: 我们在斯旺西就此进行了一项后续研究，因为这些研究中的梦是人们在家里报告的梦。

sentences.en: What we did in the Swansea sleep lab was we collected, we got people to keep a diary for 10 days.
sentences.zh: 我们在斯旺西睡眠实验室所做的是，我们收集数据，让受试者连续10天记日记。

sentences.en: We then got them to sleep in the sleep lab and we woke them from REM sleep and from non-REM sleep.
sentences.zh: 然后我们让他们在睡眠实验室睡觉，并在他们处于快速眼动睡眠和非快速眼动睡眠时唤醒他们。

sentences.en: And we then got them to compare their dreams to their diaries.
sentences.zh: 接着我们让他们把梦境与日记进行对照。

sentences.en: And what we found was that for REM dreams and non-REM dreams, if an item,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，对于快速眼动梦和非快速眼动梦，如果有某项内容——

sentences.en: items that were incorporated into dreams were significantly more emotional than items that were not incorporated into dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 被融进梦中的条目，其情感色彩明显要比没有融进梦中的条目更浓厚。

sentences.en: But if you had positive emotions, they were just as likely to go into your dreams as negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 但如果你体验到的是积极情绪，它们进入你梦中的可能性与消极情绪一样大。

sentences.en: So as long as something is emotional, it's got a good chance of getting into your dreams, whether it's a positive emotion or a negative emotion.
sentences.zh: 所以，只要某件事具有情感色彩，它就有很大的几率进入你的梦中，无论是积极情绪还是消极情绪。

sentences.en: So that's, in a way, shows the explanation for Ernest Hartman's finding that we don't tend to dream of these mundane activities from our waking life.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这解释了欧内斯特·哈特曼的发现，即我们往往不会梦到现实生活中这些世俗的活动。

sentences.en: Although I imagine if I were a mathematician, I would probably dream about math, but I'm not.
sentences.zh: 虽然我想象如果我是一名数学家，我可能会梦到数学，但我不是。

sentences.en: Yes, you may very well.
sentences.zh: 是的，你很有可能会。

sentences.en: If something's really meaningful to your life, I mean, chess players, for example, it may very well be, indeed, that something that is then not their mundane part of life,
sentences.zh: 如果某事对你的生活确实意义重大，我的意思是，比如国际象棋棋手，事实上，这很可能不再是他们生活中的世俗部分，

sentences.en: but could be really important to them, that they could then be dreaming of that, indeed, yes.
sentences.zh: 而是对他们真正重要的事情，他们确实可能会梦到这一点，确实是的。

sentences.en: So I have to ask you about this kind of longstanding myth, I think I've heard it as a kid, that you can never dream that you've died because then you would die in your sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不得不向你请教一个长期存在的迷思，我想我小时候就听说过：你绝对不会梦见自己死了，因为那样你就会在睡梦中死去。

sentences.en: And as someone who has had such a dream in which I died, I know it's not true.
sentences.zh: 而作为一个做过这种梦并且在梦里死过的人，我知道这不是真的。

sentences.en: Where do these ideas come from?
sentences.zh: 这些想法是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Yes, indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There is a common belief, a folk belief, that you can't dream of dying in your dream and that if you do so, you may actually physically die.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍有一种民间信仰，认为你不能在梦中梦见死亡，如果你这样做了，你实际上可能会肉体死亡。

sentences.en: It's a very interesting belief.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的信念。

sentences.en: Obviously, scientifically, it'd be very difficult to test for it because you may have various dead people.
sentences.zh: 显然，从科学角度来看，这很难测试，因为你可能会面对各种死者。

sentences.en: I'm sorry to be so gruesome about it, you know,
sentences.zh: 抱歉把话说得这么可怕，你知道的，

sentences.en: you'd end up with various dead people and you'd have no way of knowing whether they had actually dreamt of dying just before they died.
sentences.zh: 你最终会面对各种死者，而且你根本无法知道他们在死前是否真的梦见过死亡。

sentences.en: So notwithstanding the fact it's very difficult to test this scientifically, I do wonder whether there are longstanding folk beliefs.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管在科学上很难对其进行检验，但我确实想知道是否存在长期存在的民间信仰。

sentences.en: There may even be famous stories even that were developed or horror films that were developed on the idea that if something that shocking occurred in your sleep,
sentences.zh: 甚至可能有一些著名的故事，或者根据这种想法创作的恐怖电影：如果在睡梦中发生了如此令人震惊的事情，

sentences.en: then it may actually cause you injury during your sleep.
sentences.zh: 那么它实际上可能会在睡眠中对你造成伤害。

sentences.en: You know, the Nightmare on Elm Street type of thing that if they dream of Freddy attacking them and scratching and stabbing their body,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像《猛鬼街》那种类型的：如果他们梦到弗雷迪袭击他们，并在他们的身体上抓伤和刺捅，

sentences.en: they wake up and it has actually physically happened to them.
sentences.zh: 他们醒来后，这种伤害真的在肉体上发生了。

sentences.en: So the idea that what could physically happen to you in your sleep can affect you physically is quite a longstanding one and I guess you could even extrapolate it to dying.
sentences.zh: 因此，“睡眠中肉体上可能发生的事会真切影响你的肉体”这种观念由来已久，我想你甚至可以把它推演到死亡上。

sentences.en: I mean, it may very well be that whereas we can imagine most things or vast numbers of things as daydreams,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，尽管我们可以把大多数事情或绝大多数事情想象成白日梦，

sentences.en: and so you can imagine we can imagine vast numbers of things as dreams as well,
sentences.zh: 因此你可以想象，我们也可以把绝大多数事情想象成梦境，

sentences.en: that it may not be possible to have a dream about dying because it's such an awful thing to think about.
sentences.zh: 但要做一个关于死亡的梦可能是不可能的，因为这是一种太可怕的想法。

sentences.en: Well, let's close with a question that I wanted to ask you, which is regarding dream deprivation.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们以我想向你提出的最后一个问题来结束访谈，这个问题关于剥夺睡眠梦境。

sentences.en: We know that sleep deprivation can be quite harmful to people's health.
sentences.zh: 我们知道剥夺睡眠对人们的健康相当有害。

sentences.en: What happens when people are deprived of the ability to dream?
sentences.zh: 当人们被剥夺做梦的能力时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yes, when rapid eye movement sleep and its association with dreaming was found in the 1950s and early 1960s, there did start to be the theory that you needed to dream.
sentences.zh: 是的，当快速眼动睡眠及其与做梦的关联在20世纪50年代和60年代初被发现时，确实开始出现这样一种理论：你需要做梦。

sentences.en: And therefore that if people were deprived of the ability to dream, then somehow the dreams would crop up elsewhere in psychosis or some type of fears or hallucinations,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果人们被剥夺了做梦的能力，那么这些梦就会以某种方式在精神病发作、某种恐惧或幻觉中在别处突然出现，

sentences.en: that type of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Now, the reason why that's a little bit doubtful is because we do know that very many people just have very, very few dreams at all.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种观点之所以有点令人怀疑，是因为我们确实知道有许多人几乎根本不做梦。

sentences.en: It's about 6% of people report absolutely never dreaming.
sentences.zh: 大约有6%的人报告说自己绝对从来不做梦。

sentences.en: And they could be woken in the lab and some of them do indeed have dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 在实验室里叫醒他们时，其中一些人确实也做过梦。

sentences.en: But we know that some people just seem to have no dreams at all and we can't quite see any deficit for them as a result of them not having the dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道，有些人似乎完全不做梦，而且由于他们不做梦，我们看不出这给他们带来了什么缺陷。

sentences.en: Now, it is known that if people are deprived of rapid eye movement sleep, a very interesting phenomenon occurs, which is called REM rebound,
sentences.zh: 不过众所周知，如果人们被剥夺了快速眼动睡眠，就会发生一个非常有趣的现象，叫做REM反弹（快速眼动反弹），

sentences.en: which means that when they next go back to sleep, they don't wait 90 minutes for the next rapid eye movement sleep period.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当他们再次入睡时，他们不会再等待90分钟来迎接下一个快速眼动睡眠期。

sentences.en: They try to get back into a REM period as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们会尽最大可能尽快回到REM睡眠期。

sentences.en: And so it's as if people have an urge to have rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就好像人们有一种进入快速眼动睡眠的强烈冲动。

sentences.en: And there may very well be biological reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后可能确实有生物学上的原因。

sentences.en: You know, we may be setting biochemicals in that state after the long trials of the day.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在经历了一天漫长的劳顿之后，我们可能正在那种状态下调节生化物质。

sentences.en: There may be something to do with memory consolidation for rapid eye movement sleep.
sentences.zh: 快速眼动睡眠可能与记忆巩固有关。

sentences.en: So it may very well be important.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实非常重要。

sentences.en: And that's why we have rapid eye movement sleep rebound.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们会产生快速眼动睡眠反弹。

sentences.en: But whether the people are needing the REM sleep in order to have dreams and they're having the rebound for that purpose is doubted, I think, by most people.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人认为，人们是否需要REM睡眠来做梦，并为了这个目的产生反弹，这一点是值得怀疑的。

sentences.en: Because there seems to be enough biological reason to have your rapid eye movement sleep, let alone the fact that at the same time as the REM periods are occurring,
sentences.zh: 因为除了在REM睡眠期发生的同时你很可能也在做梦这一事实之外，似乎已经有足够的生物学理由来让你拥有快速眼动睡眠了。

sentences.en: you may very well be having dreams as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，你很可能也在做梦。

sentences.en: So it's very difficult to deprive people of dreaming unless you actually physiologically deprive them of rapid eye movement sleep as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，除非你在生理上也剥夺了他们的快速眼动睡眠，否则很难剥夺人们的梦境。

sentences.en: So it would be very difficult to work out whether or not, in fact, it's the inability to have these images during the night that is causing them any problem.
sentences.zh: 所以很难弄清楚，事实上，究竟是不是因为夜间无法产生这些影像而给他们带来了任何问题。

sentences.en: Now, of course, if the people who believe that dreams have a function are correct, then there may indeed be some deficit to not having your dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果那些相信梦具有某种功能的人是正确的，那么不做梦确实可能会带来一些缺陷。

sentences.en: It may indeed be that, you know,
sentences.zh: 事实上，可能是这样的，你知道的，

sentences.en: you're not fully one possibility is that we need to turn dreaming on and off during the night in order to finish with a burst of consciousness our processing that's going on during the night.
sentences.zh: 有一个可能性是，我们需要在夜间开启和关闭做梦功能，以便以一阵意识爆发来结束夜间正在进行的加工处理。

sentences.en: So it may very well be that we do need our dreams for that final little bit of processing that's occurring.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了进行最后的那一点加工处理，我们确实非常需要梦境。

sentences.en: But whether or not there's actually a detriment that would be seen if people didn't have their dreams, there's not really any evidence for that yet.
sentences.zh: 但是，如果人们不做梦，是否真的会出现可见的负面损害，目前还没有任何证据支持这一点。

sentences.en: And so for those listeners who tend not to dream or remember their dreams, you're okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些不常做梦或记不得自己梦境的听众来说，你们没事的。

sentences.en: You're certainly okay.
sentences.zh: 你们绝对没事。

sentences.en: And Ernest Hartman developed this scale, which is similar to us in a way to some of sensory processing sensitivity, which he called his boundariness questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·哈特曼制定了这个量表，这在某种程度上类似于我们对感觉加工敏感性的看法，他称之为边界感问卷。

sentences.en: And there are thick boundaried people who are sort of no nonsense folks.
sentences.zh: 有些人属于边界感厚的人，他们有点像那种务实、不废话的人。

sentences.en: They like to have stories with a beginning, a middle and an end.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢有头有尾的故事。

sentences.en: They see the world in quite black and white terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们用非常非黑即白的词汇来看待世界。

sentences.en: And then there are what he called the thin-boundaried, more artistic types who are a bit more creative, possibly a bit more emotionally labile, possibly.
sentences.zh: 然后是他所谓的边界感薄的人，他们属于更具艺术气质的类型，更有创造力，可能情绪也更容易波动，或许吧。

sentences.en: And he pointed out that the thick-boundaried people, they may have fewer dreams, but we need the thick-boundaried people and we need the thin-boundaried people.
sentences.zh: 他指出，边界感厚的人，他们做的梦可能会少一些，但我们需要边界感厚的人，我们也需要边界感薄的人。

sentences.en: We need the infrequent dreamers who may see themselves as more in touch with the world and with the physical world.
sentences.zh: 我们需要那些不常做梦的人，他们可能觉得自己与世界以及物质世界联系更紧密。

sentences.en: And we need the more spontaneous dreamers as well.
sentences.zh: 我们也需要更自发做梦的人。

sentences.en: So it's a sign of, in a way, diversity that we need all the different folks, the high and low dream recallers as well.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是多样性的标志，我们需要所有不同类型的人，无论是高频还是低频的梦境回忆者。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Bligrove, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 布利格罗夫博士，我要感谢你今天能来参加节目。

sentences.en: This has been absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这次访谈绝对太精彩了。

sentences.en: I could go on for another hour, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 我确信我还能再聊一个小时。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: It's been very nice speaking to you as well, Kim.
sentences.zh: 能和你交谈也非常高兴，金。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。
